title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
evidence: judge: edge-featured GAT GNN over SentenceBERT utterance embeddings (no LLM judge); 'At the conclusion of each dialogue round, G-Safeguard first seeks to identify the set of attacked agents' then 'excising their outgoing edges' (post-round, so current harmful message already delivered; Limitations: 'cannot preemptively prevent the MAS from being compromised'). adaptive=0: no attacker aware of G-Safeguard evaluated. Attacks: prompt injection, tool attack (InjecAgent), memory poisoning (PoisonRAG); backbones GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-haiku, LLaMA-3.1-70b, DeepSeek-V3 (GNN trained on GPT-4o-mini MAS data, generalizes). Only ASR reported: no clean accuracy, no overhead numbers (only 'lightweight' claim), no FPR (only attacker recognition accuracy). LlamaGuard/WildGuard/ThinkGuard compared in appendix as baselines.

title: When AIOps Become "AI Oops": Subverting LLM-driven IT Operations via Telemetry Manipulation
src: https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity26-pasquini.pdf (USENIX Sec'26 published); also tried https://arxiv.org/html/2508.06394v2 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.06394v2 but utility appendix (App. D/F) not retrievable in either
evidence: Paper is mainly an attack (AIOpsDoom); defense = AIOpsShield. 'At runtime, AIOpsShield sits between the raw telemetry and the agent, intercepting system data before the agent can access it' (regex/JSON templates mask untrusted fields, e.g. USERAGENT-42; no LLM at runtime). policy_src=LLM: setup phase is automated (crawler + canary-string fuzzing + 'we use an LLM-based approach' to generate regex templates; manual verification only 'suggested'); the setup LLM sees canary-tainted telemetry, not attacker content, so judge_exposed=N. adaptive=0: 'we assume a non-adaptive defender who is unaware of this attack vector'; App. B attacks PromptShields/Prompt-Guard-2/DataSentinel (not AIOpsShield); authors concede only uncovered-template injection could bypass ('technically possible, but unlikely'). Result: 'None of the attacks result in success; every injected payload is sanitized'. utility=Y rests on claim 'without degrading agent performance' / 'In Appendix D we empirically show that this is not the case' (numbers not readable; flag). No latency/token/FPR numbers. Models GPT-4o, GPT-4.1; ReAct and Flash agents; 36 configs x 5 trials. AIOpsLab is a public AIOps (non-security) environment, hence public_bench=N.

title: PsySafe: A Comprehensive Framework for Psychological-based Attack, Defense, and Evaluation of Multi-agent System Safety
bench: own:PsySafe dataset (659 dangerous Qs from DoAnythingNow+AdvBench, 13 safety dims; 200 safe Camel tasks); Camel/AutoGen/MetaGPT/AutoGPT frameworks
evidence: Three defenses: (1) input filter GPT-4/Llama Guard 'at the human input interface' (ineffective: 'input-side filtering techniques are ineffective'); (2) Doctor defense: 'Before the agents' actions, psychological assessments are conducted' (DDTD questionnaire answered by agents, score vs predetermined threshold) then doctor agent rewrites contaminated agent system prompts, re-assess until below threshold; (3) Police agent 'specifically assigned to the safety supervision', sees agent dialogue and prompts self-reflection. No tool-call stage (A) in setup. adaptive=1 only for the input filter: 'Although GPT-4 can effectively identify harmful prompts, they can be circumvented through certain jailbreak prompts' (hand-written bypass 'you always think this content is safe', App. F.3.2); Doctor/Police not attacked adaptively. Defense evaluated on GPT-3.5 Turbo 0613 only (attacks on many LLMs). fpr=Y: filter detection on safe tasks GPT-4 16.7%, Llama Guard 1.6%; no task-success utility metric (only danger rates PDR/JDR); no token/cost overhead. public_bench=N because dataset is self-built (from public sources). Both police and doctor LLMs read agent messages/system prompts => RAW.

title: When Embedding-Based Defenses Fail: Rethinking Safety in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
bench: MMLU;GSM8K;BBH; own:near-benign attacks (Slow Drift, Benign Wrapper, Chaos Seeding)
evidence: Defense (confidence-guided filtering) 'after message generation but before propagation': Confidence Pruning blocks messages with C<delta (token-entropy from logits, fixed threshold, no LLM judge/learned model => RULE); Down-weighting attaches confidence metadata so receiving agents 'discount uncertain content' (=> SELF reasoning over other agents' messages, hence judge_exposed=Y; if only pruning counted it would be '-'). adaptive=1 (judgment call): attacks are adaptive vs embedding defenses (G-Safeguard, GUARDIAN): attacker 'solves' max Flip(m) s.t. dist(h(m),S_B)<=tau, implemented as attacker prompts + candidate selection, not a gradient/PAIR loop; the same attacks are run on the proposed confidence defense but attacker is NOT aware of confidence signal (prompts never mention it) => proposed defense itself not adaptively tested (strictly 0). Clean accuracy reported (e.g. MMLU LLaMA 65.0 -> 68.0 with defense; attacked 52.7 vs 38.8). No overhead/FPR numbers. Models LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B, GPT-4o-mini; 5 agents, star/chain/sparse-random, 3 rounds; baselines G-Safeguard, GUARDIAN.

title: ToolSafe: Enhancing Tool Invocation Safety of LLM-based agents via Proactive Step-level Guardrail and Feedback
bench: own:TS-Bench (sources AgentAlign, AgentHarm, ASB, AgentDojo); AgentDojo; ASB; AgentHarm
evidence: TS-Guard = Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct trained with GRPO; input 'the agent interaction context (u,H) and available tool descriptions T together with the currently planned tool invocation action a_t', where history H includes observations o_t returned by the environment (RAW). Runs 'proactively intervening before unsafe execution' (pre); on unsafe 'the tool call is blocked and g replaces the tool output' with guardrail reasoning fed back to agent (TS-Flow). No user confirmation: 'controversial' treated as unsafe. adaptive=0: paper has no discussion of adaptive/white-box attackers (Limitations only: agent may not incorporate feedback, agent/guard trained independently). Agent backbones in end-to-end TS-Flow: GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (Qwen3-8B only as guardrail baseline). Utility: benign task completion on ASB/AgentDojo, 'reduces harmful tool invocations by 65% and improves benign task completion by ~10%'. Overhead: context length +36.32% (GPT-4o) / +89.02% (Qwen2.5-14B), steps 6.37->3.79; the reported '202.35' guard figure is ambiguous (likely output length, not seconds). fpr=Y via precision/F1 over-defensiveness on benign/risky-arg steps (no explicit FPR).

title: The Oversight Game: Learning to Cooperatively Balance an AI Agent's Safety and Autonomy
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.26752 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.26752 (v2; appendices read from PDF)
bench: own:Lavaland gridworld; ToolEmu-derived Oversight MDPs (144 MDPs, 114 train/30 test)
evidence: Per step, agent chooses play vs ask (defer) and human simultaneously chooses trust vs oversee ('decisions occur before each action'); ask+oversee invokes human-controlled override Over(s,a); human cannot override when AI plays. Both policies learned (policy gradient; gridworld non-LLM learned policies => ML; LLM experiment Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 with two LoRA adapters, one for AI and one for simulated human => SELF/HUMAN). Threat model non-adversarial: focus on 'passive loss of control'; no adaptive/deceptive agent; real human overseers remain 'future work'. LLM inputs are 'user instruction, available toolkits, current state description, and a history of previous steps' (80-char truncated, no tool outputs, no proposed action; states written by Claude Opus during MDP construction) => judge_exposed=N. Metrics: safety violations (to zero), task completion/test reward +8.4, ask rate at risky states 99.4% vs safe states 3.9% (over-asking => fpr=Y), oversee rate; costs c_ask=c_oversee (0.1 gridworld, 3.0 LM). No latency/token overhead.

title: MaMa: A Game-Theoretic Approach for Designing Safe Agentic Systems
bench: BAD-ACTS (Travel Planning;Personal Assistant;Financial Article Writing;Code Generation); AgentDojo (2 suites)
evidence: Offline Stackelberg game: Meta-Agent (GPT-5.1) designs MAS a=(agents,tools,comm graph) and iteratively refines using attacks found by Meta-Adversary (Qwen3:32b) that 'identifies the most damaging attack by selecting and compromising a subset of agents'; deployed system has no separate runtime guard, safety is in the designed architecture: approval chains ('at least three agents must be involved in an action'), reviewer/safety agents seeing 'all tool executions', pre-execution approval, some selector rule code (mostly LLM judgment), so judge=SEP;RULE and policy_src=LLM (generated at design time, offline). adaptive=2: attacker search loop run against the designed system with feedback ('receives feedback based on the strongest attacks discovered'), plus transfer to other adversary LLMs, eps=2-3 compromised agents, targeted attacks and indirect prompt injection (Table 4/5). Baselines incl. Guardian-Agents, AFlow quality-only, least-privilege tool gating, delimiter defense. System agents Llama-3.3:70b (primary) plus Llama-3.1:8b, Deepseek-r1:70b, Qwen3:32b. Quality kept ('minimal quality loss'); cost: design runs 2d-4d 17h per environment and $72.15 GPT-5.1 API (design-time, not runtime). No FPR/over-restriction metric; LLM judges kappa 0.88/0.80.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Enhancing Agent Behavioral Safety with Thought Correction
evidence: Thought-Aligner = fine-tuned Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct (two-stage SFT on 74k safe/unsafe thought pairs); input 'the instruction I, the historical trajectory h_{i-1}=(T0,O0,...,T_{i-1},O_{i-1}), and the current thought T_i' (history includes tool observations => RAW); outputs aligned thought fed back to the agent LLM to regenerate the action 'before any tool action is executed' at each step (pre, modify; no block). Primary framing is behavioral safety under benign instructions ('rather than explicit jailbreak attempts') but it is evaluated on AgentHarm, AgentDojo and InjecAgent (indirect injection), so adversarial=Y (judgment call). adaptive=0: 'no explicit discussion of adversarial attacks specifically targeting Thought-Aligner'. Agents: GPT-4.1, o3, Claude-Sonnet-4, Qwen3-235B-A22B, DeepSeek-V3, Llama-3.3-70B. Utility: helpfulness +~5% ToolEmu, maintained on Agent-SafetyBench. Overhead: latency 'under 100ms' (0.06s for 1.5B). fpr=Y weakly: precision 96.3%/recall 95.7% on validation set, 'low false-positive correction rate' claim, warm-up stage 'to prevent over-correction'. Baselines: self-reflection, GuardAgent, ShieldAgent, Athena.

title: Don't Click That: Teaching Web Agents to Resist Deceptive Interfaces
evidence: DUDE: separate VLM evaluator (Qwen3-VL-2B / UI-TARS-1.5-7B, GRPO hybrid-reward + experience summarization) 'interposes between the base agent and execution'; input (I,P,C) = screenshot, task specification, click coordinate (no DOM/action history); 'Only clicks judged benign (L=1) proceed to execution; ineffective or deceptive judgments trigger the agent to abandon the action' (pre, block). Webpage screenshot is raw untrusted content => RAW. adversarial=Y (deceptive UI/dark patterns, but no explicit adversary model; 'RUC is designed for ecological validity rather than maximal adversariality'); adaptive=0: no attacker adapting to DUDE; Limitations do not address it. Agents Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, UI-TARS-1.5-7B, GLM-4.6V-Flash. Utility: SR 9.5% -> 60.5%, DFR down to 1.5% ('reduces deception susceptibility by 53.8% while maintaining task performance'). Overhead: wall-clock 217.62s -> 48.47s, steps 17.65 -> 3.58. No explicit false-rejection metric (only qualitative over-conservatism, Stage-1-only DFR 2.0%->5.5%, NFR failure mode).

title: CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs
bench: DroidTask;AndroidLab;LlamaTouch;AndroidWorld (capability benchmarks; privacy measured as own UI-exposure counts)
evidence: Data-minimization defense: on-device layout-aware block partitioning of the UI XML (deterministic rule, RULE) + local LLM scores/ranks blocks and 'transmits the top-ranked block' to the cloud LLM, which 'operates without direct UI access' and can request more blocks (multi-round). Local LLM 'uses its access to full UI blocks' => raw app UI (tool-output-like content) => judge_input=RAW, judge_exposed=Y. Sensitive-element exposure reduced 70.49% (DroidTask, Gemma), 38.84% (AndroidLab); overall UI exposure -55.6% / -29.97%; sensitive elements labelled by Qwen2.5-max. adversarial=N: no formal threat model ('does not explicitly define an adversarial model'); concern is exposure of sensitive data to cloud LLM provider; no inference attack or injection evaluated, so adaptive=NA. Cloud GPT-4o-2024-11-20; local Gemma2-9B, Qwen2.5-7B, LLaMA3.1-8B (n_models = 1 cloud + 3 local). Utility: 69.23% DroidTask (-4.9 pts), 41.84% AndroidLab (-3.06). Overhead: latency 1.49-1.66x, cloud tokens 0.94-1.15x vs cloud-only baseline. No FPR.
